\section{Purpose and Scope}
This document defines the MCV Lab standard for running machine learning experiments in a scalable, reproducible, and collaborative way.

\section{Core Principles}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{P\arabic*.}, leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{No code edits for experiments.}
    \item \textbf{Full reproducibility.} Save resolved config and command.
    \item \textbf{Traceability.} Run dirs contain checkpoints, logs, configs.
    \item \textbf{Scalability.} Supports sweeps and automation (bash/SLURM/Hydra).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Standard Run Output Structure}
\begin{lstlisting}
project/
  runs/
    <run_name>/
      config.json OR config_resolved.yaml
      cmd.txt
      checkpoints/
        last.ckpt
        best.ckpt
      logs/
\end{lstlisting}

\section{Argparse Standard (Baseline)}
Use argparse for small projects; include: run naming, --config support, seed/determinism, output dirs, checkpoints.

\section{Hydra Standard (Recommended)}
Hydra is recommended for scalable projects: config groups (dataset/model/optim/trainer), composability, and multirun sweeps.

\section{SLURM Standard (HPC Execution)}
Use scripts/ with logs to slurm_logs/ and outputs to runs/. Prefer arrays for sweeps; use torchrun for DDP.

\section{Checklists}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Runs end-to-end without code edits
  \item Saves resolved config + cmd
  \item Saves checkpoints (best/last)
  \item SLURM scripts request resources explicitly and log metadata
\end{itemize}
